pr_title: speed: Always use the EVP APIs for speed measurements
pr_body:
Also drop code to handle platforms without SIGALRM (except for Windows) as the code was uncompilable anyway.

There could be further refactoring and cleanups done, but I am not sure it is worth it.

Also some of the choices made were done so the speed measurement is as close to 1.1.1 as possible to keep the values roughly comparable.

Fixes #13909
pr_comments:
I'm inclined to agree that it's not worth further refactoring.  Speed is a kludge.

The `no-deprecated` build error is relevant.

I think this should show up in NEWS because it will be user-visible.  Something like:
```
The speed command now always uses the EVP API. This will result in different performance numbers from
previous releases. When comparing, please make sure to the use -evp flag on older releases.
```

> I think this should show up in NEWS because it will be user-visible. Something like:
> 
> ```
> The speed command now always uses the EVP API. This will result in different performance numbers from
> previous releases. When comparing, please make sure to the use -evp flag on older releases.
> ```

I'll add something. Although it is not fully comparable with -evp in case of ciphers because the -evp code does something different for them.  You need to still use -evp on both old and new release for the comparison to be as close as possible.
On the other hand the implementation actually tries to be as close as possible when comparing the old and new numbers without -evp. So I am not even sure this warrants a NEWS entry. CHANGES should be sufficient.
Other than nits, this is good enough
Just rebased to fix trivial conflict in CHANGES.md. No other changes. No need to re-approve IMO.

24 hours has passed since 'approval: done' was set, but as this PR has been updated in that time the label 'approval: ready to merge' is not being automatically set.  Please review the updates and set the label manually.
Merged to master. Thank you for the reviews.

issue_context.title: Speed must not use low level crypto APIs including EVP_PKEY API to test RSA, DSA, and ECDSA
issue_context.body: DH, ECDH, and SM2 are already using EVP_PKEY. RSA, DSA, and ECDSA are remaining to be converted.
comments: Speed should be updated to use EVP for all crypto

review_comments: Add a blank line after this (I assume you'll look around for all other spots where you haven't added a blank line after the variable definitions)
Should these CPP conditional lines be removed?
I'd probably need to add some pre-checking code to avoid errors with openssl speed ecdsa in the no-ec2m builds. Not sure it is worth it.
This would fail after the fetch.  I keep forgetting that about the EC algorithms.

I had the exact same thought.  Considering that the presence of diverse algorithms is much more dynamic, having these guards in applications make less and less sense.  Generally speaking, this was already true since ENGINEs learned to do EVP level stuff, and `openssl speed` does take an `-engine` option.

However, I think this can be left for another PR, perhaps one that introduces the possibility to specify providers (and oh boy, I can see that lead to other mods, and we'll end up with a very different speed app)
This was actually a regression in master.
It is one way to speed it up also :)
A comment on the line saying that it was done on purpose might have been good..
As the wrong 4092 value was just a regression in master (the 1.1.1 code does not have it), I do not think a comment is needed.
